source_receipts.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
source_receipts.authority_reason: The authors' original LLaVA paper hosted by arXiv; author names, title and v2 date were checked on the original first page.
source_receipts.inspection_note: Personally read the original first page, section 4.1 p.4 equation (1) and surrounding text, section 4.2 p.5 Stage 1, and section 5.1 p.6 Quantitative Evaluation. The extracted PDF contains long figure serialization strings, which were excluded from the cited text inspection. The paper supports trained projection into the LLM word embedding space and checking generated answers; it does not establish the local course model's red/blue ability or a universal diagnostic theorem.

source_receipts.inspection_note: Read lines 53–145: y=xA^T+b, final-axis input/output shape, (out,in) weight and output bias, reset_parameters uniform initialization and forward F.linear. The current installed version was compared byte-for-byte with this source; no reliance on a newer unpinned documentation page.

source_receipts.title: PyTorch no_grad original context manager
source_receipts.authority_reason: Original PyTorch project source at the installed wheel's git revision; downloaded bytes exactly match the installed module.
source_receipts.inspection_note: Read lines 22–90: no_grad disables gradient recording for ordinary operations and restores prior grad state at context exit. The factory exception is explicit. This supports using zero_ inside the context; it is not an optimizer update or a training event.

source_receipts.title: PyTorch default norm original implementation
source_receipts.authority_reason: Original PyTorch project source at the installed wheel's git revision; downloaded bytes exactly match the installed module.
source_receipts.inspection_note: Read norm lines 1734–1807 and CPU dispatch lines 1841–1874. The default p='fro', dim=None computes over all elements, and this strided CPU route uses vector_norm with p=2. For (1,8) this is exactly the eight-component L2 length. The legacy norm API is deprecated in the official text, but supported in this installed execution; no change was required to verify the lesson.
